metaDescription: Six short clips from everyday rostering: sick leave, holiday wishes, constraints, the monthly plan, team mails, retirements. How it looks in Klacks.
hero.title: Stories from everyday rostering
hero.subtitle: Six situations everyone in rostering knows, and how they look in Klacks. No clip is longer than two and a half minutes, and none needs spoken words.
note: The comic scenes were created with AI. The screen recordings show Klacks with demo data.
music: Music: "Local Forecast - Elevator", Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 3.0, creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0
clip.sick-week.title: Monday. Elsa is out for the whole week.
clip.sick-week.text: Five shifts, five gaps. Klacks proposes a replacement for every day, as a scenario. Where nobody fits, Klacks says so openly.
clip.holiday-wishes.title: December. Everyone wants Christmas off.
clip.holiday-wishes.text: The vacation wishes sit in the absence calendar and appear in the roster as bars. One right-click adopts a wish as an absence.
clip.keywords.title: Mia wants the 18th off. Jonas no nights.
clip.keywords.text: Such constraints are keywords in the plan. Automatic planning keeps to them and creates the draft plan as a scenario.
clip.month-plan.title: Ten people, one site around the clock, an empty month.
clip.month-plan.text: One click starts automatic planning. The proposal is created as a scenario, the original roster stays unchanged.
clip.team-mails.title: Four team mails. No time.
clip.team-mails.text: Sandra asks Klacksy to enter the mails. Afterwards the availabilities are in the calendar and in the roster.
clip.retirement.title: The baby boomers are retiring. The work stays.
clip.retirement.text: Two experienced colleagues leave the office. Sandra says what needs to be done. Klacksy does the work by the rules of the business, Sandra checks it.
